category_title: Latino students whose disruptive or defiant behavior is interpreted as 'uncharacteristic'
minimal_context: The class is transitioning to Mr. Beattie's classroom and the students are asked to line up quietly.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to transition to Mr. Beattie's classroom. Everyone needs to line up and be quiet.

STUDENT: (Refuses to line up)

TUTOR: I still hear people talking!

STUDENT: We're going on strike!

TUTOR: Please get in line so we can leave.

STUDENT: (Singing) Oakdale school, is not the best school for you. I hate Oakdale, I hate Oakdale.

options.A: Apply increasingly serious disciplinary measures if the issue continues, such as classroom suspension, detention, and school suspension.
options.B: Have the student complete reflective journal entries in which they are encouraged to write or draw freely on their experience.
options.C: Display evidence of student goals, work samples, and achievements around the room, as well as numerous photographs of the students.
options.D: Review a behavior tracking sheet with the student and have them count all of the positive and negative marks that are circled.
